bug_semantics: Apache Airflow's serialization layer (BaseSerialization in airflow/serialization/serialized_objects.py) reconstructed exception nodes (DAT.AIRFLOW_EXC_SER / DAT.BASE_EXC_SER) by calling `import_string(exc_cls_name)` — and for the builtins variant `import_string(f"builtins.{exc_cls_name}")` — on a class name taken from the serialized blob, then instantiating it with args/kwargs from the same blob, with no restriction on what could be imported. An operator's `executor_config` reaches that decode branch, so a DAG author could place a value that causes an arbitrary callable to be imported and invoked (e.g. subprocess.check_output, builtins.eval). The code runs in the Scheduler (reconstructing serialized DAGs in its normal loop, no request involved) and in the API server on any authenticated DAG read such as GET /api/v2/dags/{dag_id}/details (CWE-502 Deserialization of Untrusted Data).
flaw_origin: Commit b365cbd8ea5fbf79e30bb2c2c058a92c4a45ab3b ("Provide mechanism to serialize airflow exceptions (#39187)", 2024-04-23, author Daniel Standish <15932138+dstandish@users.noreply.github.com>, committer GitHub, human AIP-44 prerequisite message) introduced both encode and decode sides; the decode side wrote `exc_cls = import_string(f"airflow.exceptions.{exc_cls_name}")` followed by `return exc_cls(*args, **kwargs)` — importing a name carried in the blob and calling it. Parent eba12409a7 lacks the AIRFLOW_EXC_SER branch entirely. The design (blob-controlled class name resolved by import_string) is born here; later versions generalized it (unprefixed import_string at line 667 and `import_string(f"builtins.{exc_cls_name}")` at line 669 of the pre-fix tree) without changing the defect.
